Armley residents encouraged to join community litter picks

October 8, 2026
0
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
WhatsApp

    By Helen Fay

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 1:51
    Instaread

    The members of Armley & New Wortley’s Pride in Place Neighbourhood Board are organising three community litter picks to take place over the next couple of weeks. 

    Members of the board will be out and about litter picking across the local area and local residents have been invited to take part. There will be three litter picks on the following dates:

    • Friday, 9 October – Ley Lane area litter pick, meeting at 10am at Armley Hub.
    • Saturday, 10 October  – Gilpins area litter pick, meeting at 10am at New Wortley Community Centre.
    • Saturday, 17 October – Burnsalls area litter pick, meeting at 10.30am at Yum Community Pantry.

    After each of the litter picks refreshments will be provided back at the meeting points, giving residents an opportunity to meet members of the Neighbourhood Board to ask questions and share their thoughts about what the Pride in Place Government funding can be spent on to benefit their local communities. The ‘meet the board’ events afterwards are open to all local residents.

    Reverend Phil Arnold, chair of the Armley & New Wortley Neighbourhood Board posted a video on the Pride in Place Facebook page, saying: “A reminder that Friday, 30 October at 12pm is the deadline for the Quick Wins round, where you can apply for up to £7,500 for projects that you think are really important in Armley and New Wortley. So please do contact us by e-mail, we can send you an application form.” 

    For further information, to discuss ideas or to request an application form, email: prideinplace.armley@leeds.gov.uk

    The Pride in Place Programme has been rolled out to almost 250 areas across the UK.  Armley and New Wortley will receive up to £20 million of funding and support over the next 10 years to make long-term improvements that residents want.
